items.stem: Under activity-based costing, overhead is assigned to products on the basis of:

options.text: Cost drivers that cause the activities consumed by each product
options.rationale: Correct: ABC traces overheads to activities and then to products using cause-and-effect cost drivers.
That is traditional absorption costing, which ABC is designed to improve on.

options.text: The sales value of each product
options.rationale: Sales value is an arbitrary base that ignores actual resource consumption.

options.text: An equal share across all product lines
options.rationale: Equal allocation ignores differing activity consumption and distorts costs.

items.explanation: Correct: ABC traces overheads to activities and then to products using cause-and-effect cost drivers.

items.stem: A division has an asset base of 1,000 and operating profit of 150. Head office's cost of capital is 12%. What is the division's residual income?

options.rationale: 150 is operating profit before the capital charge is deducted.
120 is the imputed capital charge, not residual income.
18 misreads the figures; the charge is 120, giving residual income of 30.

items.stem: Select TWO relevant cash flows for a short-term make-or-buy decision.

options.text: Incremental variable production costs that would be avoided by buying
options.rationale: Correct: avoidable incremental costs are relevant to the decision.

options.text: Opportunity cost of using freed-up capacity
options.rationale: Correct: the contribution forgone or gained from the freed capacity is a relevant opportunity cost.
Sunk costs are not relevant to a future decision.

options.text: Apportioned fixed head-office overhead that will not change
Historic cost of machinery already owned
options.rationale: Historic cost is sunk and irrelevant.

items.explanation: Correct: avoidable incremental costs are relevant to the decision.
